SPORTS & SCIENCE:

A Mississippi grand jury has found no criminal wrongdoing in the death of 18-year-old Nolan Wells, who disappeared during a Fourth of July trip to Horn Island. The teen’s body was discovered off the coast two days later, with the grand jury concluding his death was consistent with drowning.

The 23-member panel reviewed testimony from 43 witnesses and various evidence types. They dismissed public allegations about racial motivation or criminal conduct involving boat passengers, stating such claims were driven by public speculation rather than facts.

Wells’ friends reported he chose to stay on the island to speak with a girl, though his parents disputed this, saying he always stayed with the group. A private autopsy had listed his cause of death as undetermined pending further investigation.

The district attorney emphasized there was no evidence supporting racial motivations and noted the body’s position and condition aligned with drowning. The family’s attorney criticized the findings as raising more questions than answers, urging continued investigation.

The case highlights how quickly public perception can overshadow factual investigation, with authorities balancing community concerns against legal standards of proof.

article.title: Grand jury declines to indict anyone in the death of Mississippi teen Nolan Wells
